title: Where on Earth is Utopia now?
gist: Rhodri Lewis reviews three new books on Thomas More's Utopia and utopianism, arguing More's 1516 text was a deliberately playful, irresolvable paradox rather than a political blueprint, and warning that an age hungry for simple solutions (e.g. Peter Thiel's techno-apocalyptic readings of Bacon) misreads utopias. He praises Hadfield and Paul's More biography, finds Wren's The Uses of Utopia disappointing and Mann's The Forms of Utopia over-formalist.

insights.claim: Thomas More's Utopia (1516) was built on unresolvable playful paradox, written for readers trusted to supply their own judgement rather than to accept a programme for an ideal society.
insights.speaker: Rhodri Lewis
insights.so_what: Ideal-society narratives that present clean answers misread their own founding text; treat policy 'blueprints' with scepticism.
insights.quote: animated by a spirit of relentlessly playful paradox

insights.claim: More's Utopians depend on a slave class for their work-life balance and delegate butchery to slaves to preserve a compassionate self-image, showing utopian virtue achieved at serious cost to human dignity.
insights.speaker: Rhodri Lewis
insights.so_what: A reminder that systems marketed as frictionless often hide displaced costs onto an underclass.
insights.quote: they like eating meat but delegate responsibility for butchery to their slave class

insights.claim: Over 500 years most readers of Utopia have fled its complexity, recruiting it to justify communism, colonialism, civic planning, population control and penal reform.
insights.speaker: Rhodri Lewis
insights.quote: most of those who have engaged with Utopia over the past 500 years have fled from its complexity

insights.claim: The author argues the link between utopian writing and eugenics is well established, citing Charlotte Perkins Gilman, Aldous Huxley and Ernest Callenbach's Ecotopia.
insights.speaker: Rhodri Lewis
insights.so_what: Utopian engineering of society historically slides toward coercive population control; watch for that drift in modern techno-utopian programmes.

insights.claim: The optimism of early-1510s northern Europe collapsed within two decades of Luther's 95 theses: shared outlook, free discussion and trust in readers could no longer be assumed.
insights.speaker: Rhodri Lewis
insights.so_what: Analogy for how a single ideological rupture can rapidly polarise discourse and kill open debate.
insights.quote: Communality of outlook could no longer be assumed; discussion could no longer be free; readers could no longer be trusted.

insights.claim: Lewis argues the mid-2020s, with their stridency and hunger for simple solutions to complicated problems, are a poor climate for reading utopias, citing Peter Thiel and his followers pairing Bacon's New Atlantis with the manga One Piece to argue the hour of the Antichrist is at hand.
insights.speaker: Rhodri Lewis
insights.so_what: Signals cultural criticism of tech-billionaire ideology; relevant to reputational and political risk around Thiel-linked ventures.

insights.claim: TJ Clark's quip that utopian writing was 'the invention of early modern civil servants' frames utopianism as a display of planners' virtuosity rather than concern for real people.
insights.speaker: Rhodri Lewis
insights.so_what: Lens for evaluating technocratic or planner-led reform agendas.
insights.quote: the invention of early modern civil servants

themes.theme: Verdicts on three new utopia books

insights.claim: Andrew Hadfield and Joanne Paul's Thomas More: Humanism and Heresy is judged accessible and authoritative, particularly strong on Utopia's resistance to easy interpretation.
insights.speaker: Rhodri Lewis
insights.locator: A new study of More’s life

insights.claim: Joad Raymond Wren's The Uses of Utopia rightly warns against reading utopias as blueprints but then reads More's Utopia as a political-practical good society, mistranslating servi as 'bondmen' and so ultimately disappoints.
insights.speaker: Rhodri Lewis
insights.quote: servi not only can be translated as “slaves”, but in this context must be

insights.claim: Jenny Mann's The Forms of Utopia argues utopias are self-enclosed recursive forms akin to the Liar's Paradox and Gödel-style formal systems; Lewis finds the idea good but pushed too far into analytical imperative.
insights.speaker: Rhodri Lewis
insights.quote: a literary form that, by design, cannot be aligned to stable political content
